content:
oliver: Quick thread to settle wiring for SoftOpen probes and how FlowGate should bias traffic during a gradual canary rollback. Need concrete rules before we update the orch.

tara: Summary of the ask: when a variant enters SOFT_OPEN we should still send a fraction of traffic to it for probes, but avoid amplifying cost or autoscaler churn. Decide sampling strategy + signal annotation.

li: Proposal A: deterministic hashing per-session to keep probe QPS stable (e.g., 2% of sessions). Pros: stable signal, easy to reconcile. Cons: can miss short-lived spikes if unlucky.

ben: Proposal B: time-decayed probabilistic sampling with EWMA-adjusted probability. Pros: adapts to traffic changes; Cons: more noisy and potentially harder to replay.

oliver: I prefer deterministic per-session sampling for SOFT_OPEN probes. If we tie sampling to session_id hash + tenant salt we get reproducible coverage and easy debugging.

tara: Agree on deterministic sampling for probes. But for emergency canary rollback we also want a small percentage of additional ad-hoc probes to check recovery after config changes. Those can be probabilistic. 

li: That suggests hybrid: deterministic baseline (configurable per-tenant) + ephemeral probabilistic burst for recovery checks. Keep burst capped (max 0.5% absolute of traffic).

ben: Important: annotate probe requests with flowgate_probe=true and probe_origin={deterministic|burst}. Control plane needs to ignore probe traffic when computing autoscaler metrics or at least downweight it.

oliver: How should FlowGate expose these annotations? Inline headers? telemetry events? I want both: short header for runtime routing and compact telemetry event for post-hoc analysis.

tara: Runtime header example: X-FlowGate-Probe: deterministic; X-FlowGate-Reason: soft_open_probe. Telemetry event: session_id, variant, probe_type, latency_ms, error_flag. No payloads.

li: Also need a safety cap: if probe error rate > 20% in 1m, immediately escalate to HARD_OPEN for that variant locally and escalate to Arbiter. That prevents long tails from killing many users.

ben: Operationally, define three escalation channels: local immediate (FlowGate), tenant-watchdog (ops), and Arbiter-escalation. FlowGate does local HARD_OPEN; Arbiter verifies and can globalize.

oliver: On Oscillation: if two nodes disagree on probe membership for the same session (due to hash salt drift), add versioned salt with TTL. FlowGate should refuse to change salt unless control plane pushes a new salt with signed version.

tara: Good call. We'll keep salt version in the config proto and allow rollback. Salt changes are infrequent and audited.

li: Concern: autoscaler sees increased fallback traffic during HARD_OPEN events and might spur extra capacity. Add a probe_flagged metric that the autoscaler subtracts from incoming rate for a short window. We'll call it flowgate_inhibit_seconds in the autoscaler contract.

ben: For per-tenant configuration: tenant can set base_probe_fraction (0.0-0.1), max_burst_fraction (0.0-0.005), and soft_open_backoff_ms (how long between probe bursts). Default base=0.02, burst=0.002, backoff=300s.

oliver: Testing: hardware-in-the-loop sim: simulate 50 tenants, each with mixtures of session lengths; inject a canary with a memory leak that causes rising latency. Validate that deterministic probes detect and that burst probes confirm recovery.

tara: Telemetry retention: keep probe events for 7d at full fidelity, then aggregate to 30d. This helps postmortems without exploding costs.

li: Security: probe headers must be authenticated within our internal network to avoid external spoofing. Also redact tenant IDs in shared telemetry views.

ben: Small nit: name change request: call the state SOFT_PROBE instead of SOFT_OPEN to reduce confusion with other systems. If we change name, update docs and enums.

oliver: Fine with SOFT_PROBE. Make sure Arbiter/FlowGate RPCs use the same enum. Version it as v1.1.

ops-bot: scheduled: softprobe/flowgate v0.9 -> canary cluster at 2026-05-10T02:00Z. CI green. :white_check_mark: 

li: Action items: tara to draft config schema for hybrid sampling; ben to add probe flags to autoscaler contract; oliver to add header + telemetry proto changes; ops to schedule sim.

oliver: OK let's lock this and fold into next RFC revision. Thanks everyone.
